headers.//: The vercel.app address serves the same site as the domain. To a search engine that is a second copy competing with the first, and the one it picks is not ours to choose. This tells crawlers to leave that copy alone. It is a header rather than a redirect on purpose: the Deriv OAuth callback is registered against a URL, and bouncing that host would break the one flow the site cannot do without.
Every preview build Vercel makes is another copy of the site on its own address. None of them should ever be indexed.
The verification file must be served as plain text, exactly as Google wrote it.
The pages behind the connection place real trades. A stale one served from a cache would be an old build talking to Deriv, so they are re-fetched every time; the assets around them are safe to keep.
Ordinary hardening. Nothing here frames another site or is meant to be framed.
